report.title: Cloud Security Assessment
report.scope: Production AWS account, customer-facing web application and CI/CD pipeline. Testing ran from 15 to 26 September 2026.

summary: We reviewed the production cloud environment and found 6 issues: 1 critical, 2 high, 2 medium and 1 low. The critical issue (a public storage bucket with shipment exports) should be fixed this week. The others can be planned over the next quarter.

findings.title: Storage bucket with shipment exports is publicly readable
findings.description: The bucket that stores nightly shipment exports allows anonymous read access. The files contain customer names and delivery addresses.
findings.recommendation: Block public access on the bucket and the account, rotate the export links already shared, and review access logs for the last 90 days.

findings.title: Root account has no MFA
findings.description: The AWS root user can sign in with a password only. It was last used 41 days ago.
findings.recommendation: Enable hardware MFA on the root user, store the device securely and alert on any root sign-in.

findings.title: Long-lived deploy keys in the CI pipeline
findings.description: The pipeline uses an IAM user access key created 14 months ago with administrator permissions.
findings.recommendation: Replace the key with short-lived OIDC credentials and a role limited to the deploy actions.

findings.title: Database snapshots are not encrypted
findings.description: Manual snapshots of the orders database are stored without encryption at rest.
findings.recommendation: Copy the snapshots with encryption enabled, delete the unencrypted copies and enforce encryption by policy.

findings.title: Web application sends no security headers
findings.description: Responses lack Content-Security-Policy, Strict-Transport-Security and X-Content-Type-Options headers.
findings.recommendation: Add the headers at the load balancer or CDN and start with a report-only Content-Security-Policy.

findings.title: Audit log retention is 30 days
findings.description: Audit logs are kept for 30 days, shorter than the 1-year retention in the client's own policy.
findings.recommendation: Move audit logs to a dedicated archive bucket with a 1-year lifecycle rule.
